sentences.text: Mangalaram Rajaiah, vs The Tahsildar, on 11 November, 2024

The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.3447 Of 2010
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, seeking the following relief:
"...issue a Writ of Mandamus or any other appropriate Writ or direction declaring the action of the respondent Nos.1 to 4 in proposing to lay a road in the lands of the petitioners in Sy.Nos.130/2, 441/A, 129/1, 131/4, 130/4, 130/4, 375/A, 130/5, 130/5,
375/AA, 441/AA, 129/3, 138/4, situated at Vattinagulapalli Village, Rajendra Nagar Mandal, Ranga Reddy District and Sy.No.262/RU situated at Gopanapalli Village,
Serilingampally Manal, Ranga Reddy Distirct, without initiating proceedings under land Acquisition Act or paying compensation as illegal, arbitrary and one without jurisdiction and consequently direct the respondent Nos.1 to 4 not to dispossess the petitioners without following the due process..."
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue for the respondents.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent No.5 submits that as per the counter filed by the respondent No.5 in paragraph No.6, it is stated that the road is not built on the petitioners' land, and no part of it goes through their property.
Therefore, there is no question of any loss or interference with the petitioners' land.

SK,J W.P.No.3447 OF 2010 4. Taking into consideration the averments made in the counter-affidavit filed by the respondent No.5, the cause in the writ petition does not survive and accordingly, the writ petition is closed.

If the respondents want to acquire the land of the petitioners, they have to follow the due procedure as contemplated under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
